name: Radfeld
kurzbeschreibung: Residential and industrial community in the Unterinntal with excellent accessibility and beautiful natural surroundings along the Inn.
text:
Überblick

Radfeld is situated in the Tyrolean Lower Inn Valley within the Kufstein district at an elevation of 512 metres, home to around 2,570 residents. The municipality extends across an expansive alluvial cone on the southern banks of the Inn River, transitioning almost seamlessly into the historic glass town of Rattenberg to the west. To the north, the Inn forms the natural border with Kramsach, while the Kundler Ache enters the river to the east. Radfeld features sunny meadows, historic farmsteads, and direct access to the Mauckenwald forest, offering rural tranquility close to the Alpbachtal and Kramsach lakes.

Geschichte

Radfeld ranks among the earliest documented settlements in Tyrol. As early as 788 AD, it was recorded in Salzburg's Notitia Arnonis as ad ratfeld ecclesia cum territorio. The name derives from the Old High German personal name Rato, signifying Rato's field. In medieval times, Radfeld served as the agricultural breadbasket for the fortified merchant town of Rattenberg and operated as a bustling hub for Inn river timber rafting and navigation. The branch church of St. Briccius at Lindenbühel was built between 1484 and 1490 by master builder Gilg Sewer in Late Gothic style, showcasing intricate net vaulting, baroque altarpieces by Christoph Anton Mayr, and the historic Briccius spring.

Anreise

Radfeld provides effortless transport connections. By car, drivers take the Inntalautobahn A12 via exit Kramsach/Alpbachtal or Wörgl-West/Kundl and follow the B171 Tiroler Straße for just a few minutes. Rail passengers arrive via the Lower Inn Valley railway at the Rattenberg-Kramsach station, located only 800 metres or a ten-minute walk from the centre of Radfeld. Furthermore, frequent VVT regional buses link the village directly with Brixlegg, Rattenberg, Kundl, and surrounding communities.

Tipps

A relaxing stroll leads into the shaded Mauckenwald forest, providing cool paths and serene nature during warm summer days. Cyclists enjoy the flat, paved Inn-Radweg cycle trail along the riverbanks, ideal for leisure touring and e-bikes. Within the village, a well-maintained Kneipp water facility provides refreshing breaks. Visitors can easily walk into medieval Rattenberg to watch master glassblowers or venture to the nearby Museum Tiroler Bauernhöfe open-air heritage museum in Kramsach. In winter, dedicated ski shuttles connect directly to the Ski Juwel Alpbachtal Wildschönau ski area.
